newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland raises upper limit for '97 Eurobond issues.
newsitem.headline: Poland raises upper limit for '97 Eurobond issues.

text.p: Poland increased the upper limit for budget financing on international markets to $500 million in the 1997 budget draft from an earlier planned $300 million, a deputy finance minister said.
The ministry announced the increase after Poland's parliament passed a law lowering personal income taxes next year.
The finance ministry said the lower taxes would widen the 1997 budget deficit by 920 million zlotys to 12.2 billion.
"We are planning to finance the larger budget deficit by increasing issues of our paper on international markets," said deputy finance minister Halina Wasilewska-Trenkner.
"We set the maximum limit on the value of these bonds at $500 million," she said.
She said lower debt financing costs next year would bring additional inflows to help fill the larger gap.

Poland returned to international finance markets in 1995 with a $250 million issue and followed up this year with a 250 million German mark five-year eurobond priced at 65 basis points above comparable bunds.
Poland's rating by Moody's Investor Service is now Baa3, while that of Standard and Poor's is BBB-.
